MARKET.head: Australian white wine shipments to China more than double in third quarter
MARKET.summ: White wine export volumes to the market more than doubled, rising 143.6%, according to Wine Australia data. The growth comes as Australian producers seek a greater foothold among Chinese white wine drinkers, including consumers exploring alternatives to Burgundy
takeaways: Australian white wine export volumes to mainland China rose 143.6% in Q3 2026, per Wine Australia data.
Total Australian wine export value to mainland China rose 1.9% to A$166.33 million in the quarter, bucking a global decline.
White wine still made up only 7.14% of Australian export value to China, against 91.62% for red.

MARKET.head: Shanghai wine trader WINEXSH files for bankruptcy liquidation amid price slump
MARKET.summ: Shanghai-based fine wine trader WINEXSH has applied for bankruptcy liquidation, with a supplier reporting an unpaid order and Chinese wine media citing complaints from customers unable to collect wines or secure refunds
takeaways: Shanghai Free Trade Zone Wine Exchange Co., known as WINEXSH, applied for bankruptcy liquidation, reviewed by Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court.
The court reportedly held a hearing on the application October 29, though it is unclear whether the application was accepted.
A Bordeaux supplier said WINEXSH left its latest en primeur order unpaid, blaming falling fine wine prices and large unsold inventories.

MARKET.head: Western Australian wineries sell on the spot at Shanghai festival
MARKET.summ: A two-day Discover Western Australian Festival drew nearly 900 people in Shanghai, with exhibitors reporting stronger-than-expected consumer sales and new business prospects among distributors, restaurants and hotels
takeaways: Discover Western Australia Festival drew nearly 900 people to Bridge 8 Art Space in Shanghai on November 7-8.
Exhibitors including Ferngrove and Subsea Estate's agent reported on-site sales and expected buyer follow-up.
Most participating wineries already had importers or stock in China, letting visitors buy wines they had just tasted.

MARKET.head: Wine Australia and Wine Victoria partner on three-year Victorian industry projects
MARKET.summ: A new partnership between Wine Australia and Wine Victoria will fund a range of projects across the Victorian wine industry supporting grapegrowers and winemakers.
takeaways: Wine Australia and Wine Victoria will co-fund Victorian wine industry projects over three years, aligned with the Victorian Wine Strategy 2025-2030.
The program combines $540,000 in Victorian Government funding secured by Wine Victoria with $346,667 from Wine Australia's Australian Wine Future Fund.
Projects target sustainability, biosecurity preparedness, data-driven decisions and export capability, delivered through field days, workshops, webinars and benchmarking tools.

MARKET.head: Wine stays Australia's top-bought alcohol as drinking moderates and spending per visit rises
MARKET.summ: New research shows that wine endures as “the most widely purchased category” in Australia at 55%, followed by spirits at 46% and beer at 44%. The new ‘What’s Driving Australia’s Alcohol Shopper: Consumption, Channels, Promotions and Occasions’ report from Vypr and Shop! ANZ found that 41% of Australians are drinking less than a...
takeaways: Vypr and Shop! ANZ report: 55% of Australians buy wine, ahead of spirits at 46% and beer at 44%.
41% of Australians drink less than a year ago or have stopped, while only 6% drink more.
48% of shoppers now typically spend over $40 per liquor-store visit, up from about 23% a year ago.

MARKET.head: Marnong Estate releases first Reserve Chardonnay alongside new Sangiovese rosé
MARKET.summ: Marnong Estate has unveiled its first-ever Reserve Chardonnay as a part its new collection of cool-climate expressions from the estate's Sunbury vineyards. The 2024 Reserve Chardonnay leads the new range which features the 2025 Single Vineyard Chardonnay and 2025 Estate Chardonnay, offering “distinct interpretations of the...
takeaways: Marnong Estate, a Sunbury winery, has released its first-ever Reserve Chardonnay, the 2024 vintage, as part of a new cool-climate range.
The spring range also includes the 2025 Single Vineyard and Estate Chardonnays and the 2026 Estate Sangiovese Rosé, its first rosé from Sangiovese.
The spring releases are sold nationally through independent merchants, at the cellar door and online via the winery's website.

MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes and 23 producers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: 23 Moldovan wine and spirits producers exhibit at ProWine Shanghai from November 10 to 12 to seek Chinese importers.
Chinese customs data shows Moldovan wine imports reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026.
About 85% of Moldova's wine production is exported, with the EU taking roughly 60% of exports.

MARKET.head: Australian wine small formats gain traction amid moderation and single-person households
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined Australian 187mL single-serve wine pack sales rose 22 per cent to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39 per cent from 2023-24 to 2025-26, concentrated in Asia-Pacific markets.
Single-person households are 26 per cent of Australian households, up from 18 per cent in 1981, per Census data.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing rules restrict vague eco claims on wine labels from September 27
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: EU Directive 2024/825 (EmpCo), enforced from September 27, bans vague environmental claims such as eco-friendly and green on consumer products.
Wine producers must substantiate sustainability claims through third-party certification or verifiable data, and old stock is not grandfathered in.
Penalties are set by individual member states and can reach four percent of annual turnover for widespread violations.

MARKET.head: VinePair's weekly roundup spans Stoli, Modelo, Heineken, RNDC and Diageo news
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on Stoli’s return to the U.S., Modelo’s deal with the NCAA, the latest product releases, and more.
takeaways: VinePair's Friday Booze News Weekly Roundup gathers beverage alcohol headlines and product releases from the week.
Items cited include Stoli's return to the U.S. after bankruptcy and Modelo becoming official beer of the NCAA.
Other items cover Heineken's memo on weight-loss drugs and RNDC's Chapter 11 liquidation.

CULTURE.head: VinePair host reflects on American wine in 2026 and ways to celebrate it
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers, host of VinePair's podcast Wine 101, reflects on American wine in 2026.
The episode is sponsored by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks.

CULTURE.head: ASVO names 2026 Viticulturist and Winemaker of the Year and science award winners
CULTURE.summ: Last night, the Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) revealed the winners of its Awards for Excellence. The ASVO said the winners were chosen from a very high calibre and diverse range of submissions showing expertise across winemaking, viticulture and wine science. Highlights of the evening included the naming...
takeaways: Chris Dent, owner of Gorton Drive Estate and chair of Murray Valley Winegrowers, was named 2026 ASVO Viticulturist of the Year.
David Bicknell, almost 25 years at Oakridge Wines, was named 2026 ASVO Winemaker of the Year.
Tracey Siebert, AWRI flavour scientist with around 2,800 citations, won the Wine Science and Technology Award.

CULTURE.head: AI's energy, e-waste and water costs threaten wine's sustainability image
CULTURE.summ: The Australian and New Zealand wine sector prides itself on sustainability. The very concept has become the industry’s bread and butter, quite frankly. Look at any winery website and you’ll find a dedicated page filled with paragraphs detailing all the initiatives reducing carbon emissions, saving water and limiting energy use...
takeaways: Australian and New Zealand wine sector heavily promotes its sustainability credentials to consumers.
AI adoption in wine, from labels to social media, risks undermining that clean and green reputation.
Data centres powering AI could use large volumes of water and generate rising e-waste, per cited research.

CULTURE.head: Marlborough viticulture technician Anna Kelland wins 2026 Young Horticulturist of the Year
CULTURE.summ: Marlborough viticulture technician Anna Kelland has won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title, having “excelled” in an intensive two-day competition in Auckland from 4-5 November. Kelland was the 2025 New Zealand Young Viticulturist of the Year and therefore went through to represent the viticulture sector in this year’s...
takeaways: Anna Kelland, a viticulture technician for Constellation Brands in Marlborough, won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title in Auckland on 4-5 November.
Kelland, the 2025 New Zealand Young Viticulturist of the Year, beat four rivals from grower, arborist, amenity and plant producer sectors.
Her prizes total more than $25,000, and she is the tenth Young Viticulturist to take the overall title.

SCIENCE.head: Burgundy estate uses electrical soil mapping to guide vineyard decisions
SCIENCE.summ: Electrical conductivity maps can reveal striking differences beneath seemingly uniform vineyards, but understanding what those differences mean is far more complicated
takeaways: Domaine du Cellier aux Moines in Givry, Burgundy, used electrical conductivity mapping from 2021 to locate soil pits.
Mapping revealed limestone density differences about 1.5 meters down that were not visible from the surface.
Tressed Pinot Noir in a denser-limestone parcel reached 13.6% potential alcohol versus 14.5% for a trimmed neighbour in 2026.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI updates agrochemical lookup app on Apple and Google stores
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has released an updated version of its AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on Apple and Google app stores.
The free app gives rapid access to information in the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet, known as the 'Dog book'.
Users with the app already installed are advised to perform an update to keep receiving app updates.

NEWSLETTERS.head: An Austrian wine mini-study with seven interesting bottles
NEWSLETTERS.summ: These wines were being poured at the Star Wine List Inspiration Day in Stockholm, November 2026. Mayersistas Pet Nat Zweigelt
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Seven Austrian wines were poured at the Star Wine List Inspiration Day in Stockholm, November 2026, reviewed with scores out of 100.
Muhr's 2022 Ried Spitzerberg Obere Roterd Blaufränkisch from Carnuntum received the highest score in the set, 96/100.
Kracher's 2022 Welschriesling Trockenbeerenauslese Nummer 2 from Burgenland was described as brilliant and also scored 96/100.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Kitchen Season’s Pantry Staples
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Stocking up before the cooking starts in earnest; plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker's Maker's Table piece lists pantry staples for Kitchen Season, following her earlier list of essential kitchen tools in The Salt.
She advises checking pantry shelves in mid-November, since baking ingredients do not last indefinitely.
Spices and herbs should be refreshed regularly and bought in small quantities from bulk aisles to keep flavor at its peak.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Sixteen Austrian Wines You Should Try
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delicious recommendations,including old favourites and new discoveries
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Fischer's Sauvignon Blanc St. Anna 2025 is made by brothers Klaus and Bernard, who started making wine at the family business in 2015.
Franz Hofstätter's declassified Grüner Veltliner comes from the Achleiten vineyard in the Wachau and is uncertified organic.
Hajszan Neumann's Grüner Veltliner Natural 2025 is priced at €15 from Lebendige Weine (2023 vintage) and has 12% ABV.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics should know slightly more than their target audience, rather than being either superior tasters or obsessive facts-collectors.
Atkin says undisclosed relationships like dining or shared politics can influence reviews, and cites research that disclosure may make advisors more self-interested.
Atkin criticises wine reviewers for spending about 30 seconds assessing each wine, often in line-ups of tens or hundreds.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/8/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Meet the Young Winemakers Reshaping Burgundy Right Now
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Meet the young winemakers in the heart of Burgundy who are tending the vines and shaping the future of wine
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: William Whitehead has taken charge of Domaine Michel Rebourgeon in Pommard, which makes about 20,000 bottles a year from 4.25 hectares.
Pierre Arcelain runs Domaine Michel Arcelain, where the white wine ages 12 months in a concrete egg.
Arthur Thibert works alongside his father Pierre in Corgoloin, overseeing a new cuverie and more sustainable farming.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources such as local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction notices, and cellar consignments not well indexed by ordinary search.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions or uploaded images, and Orpheus notifies them when a matching wine is available in its network and connects them with the seller.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Bourgueil’s Aurélien Revillot
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Through a Burgundian lens, Cabernet Franc becomes a study of place and terroir, parcel by parcel
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Aurélien Revillot is a relative newcomer to Bourgueil whose domaine is part of Becky Wasserman's portfolio.
Revillot makes a blended entry-level cuvée and single-vineyard wines from his best slope parcels, with two cuvées parcellaires set to join from the 2020 vintage.
Revillot grew up in a Mâconnais farming family, trained in Dijon, worked at Domaine Drouhin in Oregon and Newton Johnson in South Africa, and staged at Domaine de la Chevalerie in 2010.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós's family, making wine since 1497, produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872 in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, Penedès.
Cava is named after the cellars dug to store the wine, a term used informally from the 1960s and formalised under Spanish law in 1972.
Sumarroca's 2022 Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava, from Finca Sumarroca in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, aged 40 months and costs $28 Cdn.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing and was set to visit Guangzhou on November 6.
Spain ranked fifth for wine volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but only a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Spain ranked sixth for value in China last year, below New Zealand, with a per-liter value only slightly above Chile.
